question.problem:
Let the joint CDF of $X$ and $Y$ be $F(x,y),$ where

$$
F(5,4)=1,\,F(5,1)=\frac{2}{9},\,F(4,4)=\frac{1}{3},\,F(4,1)=\frac{1}{9}.
$$

Find $P(4\le X\le 5,1\le Y\le 4).$
question.worked_solution:
Recall that $F(x,y)=P(X\le x,Y\le y)$ is the probability that the pair $(X,Y)$ will lie inside the infinite rectangular region that has its top-right corner at $(x,y)$ and whose sides are parallel to the coordinate axes.

Let's sketch the region corresponding to the probability we wish to find.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/differential/14211556/assets/137e3d2e3344f5d1f57f36d470564a518c359bb46d5278382b7242e73999e80e.png)

Geometrically, this region can be obtained as follows:

1\. Take the infinite rectangle that has its top-right corner at $(5,4).$

2\. Subtract the infinite rectangles that have their top-right corners at $(5,1)$ and $(4,4).$

3\. Finally, we need to *add back* the infinite rectangle that has its top-right corner at $(4,1).$ This is because we subtracted this region twice in step 2.

Therefore, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}P(4\le X\le 5,1\le Y\le 4) & =\overset{\text{top-right corner at }(5,4)}{\overset{⏞}{P(X\le 5,Y\le 4)}} \\  & \,-\overset{\text{top-right corner at }(5,1)}{\overset{⏞}{P(X\le 5,Y\le 1)}}-\overset{\text{top-right corner at }(4,4)}{\overset{⏞}{P(X\le 4,Y\le 4)}} \\  & \,+\overset{\text{top-right corner at }(4,1)}{\overset{⏞}{P(X\le 4,Y\le 1)}} \\  & =F(5,4)-F(5,1)-F(4,4)+F(4,1) \\  & =1-\frac{2}{9}-\frac{1}{3}+\frac{1}{9} \\  & =\frac{9}{9}-\frac{2}{9}-\frac{3}{9}+\frac{1}{9} \\  & =\frac{5}{9}.\end{aligned}
$$
